newsitem.title: CHILE: Foreign buyers push Chilean shares to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buyers push Chilean shares to higher close.

text.p: Chilean shares extended their bull run to new heights on heavy foreign buying and confidence in the electrical and telecom sectors, brokers said.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares ended 1.70 percent higher to 137.07 points. The all-share IGPA rose 1.26 points to 5842.30 points on strong volume of 160 million shares traded.

Brokers reported heavy demand for liquid electrical stocks, largely on a state anti-trust board's ruling late Wednesday exonerating Enersis, which had been accused of crowding out competition in the power generation business.
Enersis ended 1.6 percent higher to 306 pesos.
Its electricity generation unit Endesa was up 2.2 percent to 322 pesos and Chilectra, the group's distribution outfit, Chilectra, was up 2.2 percent to 3190 pesos.

Wall Street's run-up to a record high also contributed to the IPSA's gain, but brokers cited mainly local factors, including perceptions that Chile remains a safer bet in the long-term than more volatile markets elsewhere in Latin America.

With the IPSA already surpassing most brokerages' targets for the whole year, many analysts were reviewing their annual forecasts for the bolsa as a whole and for big-volume stocks in the energy and natural resources sectors.
But brokers cautioned that the bourse's bullish trend since mid-May, with a breather last week, was not so spectacular taking into account its mediocre performance in 1996.
"Last year we fell in real terms about 20 percent, and this year we've gone up in real terms about 30 percent, so what we really have is about a 10 percent increase," one said.

Telecom stocks were among the gainers, on optimism that a planned merger between Compaa de Telecomunicaciones de Chile and long distance competitor VTR was close to fruition, brokers said. CTC A shares were up 1.6 percent to 3770 pesos, and Entel was up 0.7 percent to 3120 pesos.

Surging copper prices boosted prices for the bourse's few mining concerns, brokers said. Mantos Blancos was up 3.9 percent to 1200 pesos, and Punta de Cobre, or Pucobre, A series was up 4.9 percent to 45,100 pesos, one of the day's biggest gainers.

Paper pulp and oil conglomerate Copec was up 2.9 percent to 1,962 pesos. Santander Investment issued a report raising its yearly earnings estimates and target prices for Copec and reiterating a buy recommendation.
Brokers said a technical breather was possible on Friday, but that they expected the bourse's bullish mood to continue for most of next week.
